chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Ismail al-Sayqal, from Abu Yahya al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the newborn is born for you, what do you do with it? I said, 'I do not know what we do with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a lentil of Jawashir, soak it in water, then drip it into his nose: two drops in the right nostril and one drop in the left. Recite the Adhan in his right ear and the Iqamah in his left. Do this before his umbilical cord is cut, for he will never be startled, nor will he be affected by Umm al-Sibyan.'

key_terms.أَقِمْ: Recite the Iqamah (second call to prayer)
key_terms.أُمُّ الصِّبْيَانِ: A spiritual affliction or entity affecting children
key_terms.جَاوَشِيرَ: A specific plant or seed used in traditional remedies

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals for a newborn in Shia tradition to ensure protection and calmness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines specific Sunnah practices for newborns, emphasizing the recitation of the Adhan in the right ear and Iqamah in the left to instill divine presence, alongside the application of Jawashir to the nostrils. These rituals are performed before the umbilical cord is severed to ensure the child remains calm and is protected from 'Umm al-Sibyan,' a spiritual affliction or jinn often associated with infancy in Shia tradition. The practice highlights the integration of physical care with spiritual safeguarding from birth.
